chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from someone else, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who married the sister of his brother from breast-feeding, he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like that I marry the sister of my brother from breast-feeding.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying the sister of one's milk-brother in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the juristic discussion surrounding the prohibition of marrying a milk-sister's sister, a specific extension of the general rule regarding milk-kinship (radha'). The Imam’s statement reflects the scholarly nuance in distinguishing between direct milk-relatives and those connected through them, illustrating the practical application of hadith in personal status law within Shia jurisprudence.
